items.title: Pay 'Branchenregister' listing fee
items.quote: Der Betrag von 569,06 € ist bis zum 16.09.2027 zu überweisen.
items.computation: The letter states an explicit calendar due date (16.09.2027) rather than a period to count, so the due date is simply that printed date. No weekend/holiday adjustment is needed to apply since this is a payment due date given directly by the sender, not a statutory deadline, and 16.09.2027 is a Thursday.

warnings: This letter matches the well-known 'Branchenregister' / fake business directory scam pattern (similar to the 'Gewerbeauskunft-Zentrale' scams): it is styled as an 'Eintragungsbestätigung und Rechnung' (invoice-like confirmation) but the fine print reveals 'Die Eintragung ist ein Angebot; mit Ihrer Zahlung nehmen Sie es an.' — i.e. it is actually just an unsolicited offer, and paying it would mean entering into a 24-month paid contract you likely never asked for.

The bank account for payment is held in the name 'BRM Verlagsservice Ltd.', which does not match the sender's own letterhead name 'Branchenregister Musterland – Verzeichnisservice' — a classic mismatch red flag.

The letter threatens to hand the matter straight to a debt-collection agency 'ohne weitere Mahnung' (without a further reminder) if the very short ~7-day deadline is missed, a pressure tactic typical of these scam mailings.

The recipient's town 'Musterlüne' and the sender's own name containing 'Musterland' look like template/placeholder text, suggesting this may be a sample or mass-mailed scam letter rather than a genuine, individually issued invoice.

Recommendation: do not pay this invoice; it is very likely a scam, and the underlying 'contract' can in most cases be contested as not validly concluded or voided for lack of a clear, prominent price disclosure (Transparenzgebot) typical of these schemes — the user should verify independently (e.g. via consumer protection agencies) before taking any action.
